verbs.name: fusion_create_library
verbs.summary: ONE-CALL library creation for web-control (one call = one consent). EVERY LIBRARY IS MULTI-PART - a single-part library is simply parts:[one entry], and there is no separate single-part verb to choose. Pass parts:[{package, lbrPath, modelPath}] for any number of parts; the older {libraryPath, stepPath} shape still works and is normalised into a one-element parts list, so both run the identical code path and the ETA scales with the part count either way. TWO entry shapes: A) {libraryPath, stepPath} - a ready .lbr plus the 3D; B) {kicadSymbolPath, kicadFootprintPath, stepPath, pinMap?} - KiCad sources; needs adom-lbr, which is Linux-container-only by platform rule, so on Windows/Mac boxes shape B refuses IMMEDIATELY (adom_lbr_unavailable, before any staging or Fusion launch - fusion_readiness reports kicadIngest up front). Convert at AUTHORING time in a container and use shape A. pinMap = explicit {pinName: padName} for when pin numbers do not match pad names (BGA-style). Chains convert -> bind 3D -> prove (four evidence frames + verdict) in the BACKGROUND and returns immediately; poll fusion_prove_result (stage narrates; top-level `verdict` proven/not_proven is the score - `stage:done` only means the chain finished). EVERY PART IS PROVED, not just the first: a 10-component library streams 40 evidence frames, FOUR per component (symbol, footprint, 3d, ganged) in assembly order, each tagged with `part` so a front end can group them as they arrive, and `provedParts[]` reports per-part pass/fail. The library is proven only if EVERY part is - one good part does not vouch for nine unchecked ones. On the FINAL fetch pass {inlineFrames:true} to get each evidence frame as a base64 thumbnailDataUrl a browser can render (plain polls return box paths only). The chain closes its library document on success AND failure - batches need no between-part sweeping. stepPath is required for a PROVEN library - no real 3D body without it.

verbs.name: fusion_demo
verbs.summary: FIRST-TIME-USER DEMO in one verb - the thing to run when someone new wants to SEE what this bridge does (HD's installer calls this). Takes them from nothing to a real board: launches Fusion, FINISHES the Autodesk sign-in - it OPENS the sign-in in the user's NATIVE browser IN THE BACKGROUND (never interrupting their work) and returns signinWhere/signinProfile/signinSession so you can tell them exactly where it is waiting, then offer three paths: they finish it, you foreground it, or (with their OK) you drive it. Native browser via ABE/nbrowser_* because that profile is already signed into Autodesk - never pup, which is anonymous, sets up APS cloud search (or explains it if declined) and runs a LIVE sample search so they see 2-second results, then opens an electronics PROJECT and walks SCHEMATIC -> 2D BOARD -> 3D BOARD, screenshotting each view to show them. STAGED + RESUMABLE: every call advances as far as it safely can and returns stage/done/narrate/screenshots plus a _hint with the exact next action; keep calling it until done:true. NEVER leave a first-time user parked on the sign-in screen - that is the failure this verb exists to prevent. See the 'fusion-demo' skill. TOUR MODE: pass {mode:'tour'} for the ASYNC guided ELECTRONICS tour (John, 2026-09-04: Adom is an electronics prototyping company, so the tour shows electronics, never a mechanical part): eight beats over the bundled sample part - the library, the symbol, the footprint, the 3D chip minted from its STEP and bound into the user's hub, then a REAL board from the user's hub (BQ25792, the Adom charger; args.board or args.boardUrn override) in schematic, 2D board and 3D board, falling back to a generated solo board only when the hub has none, and a cloud search; multipart libraries are mentioned in the narration, never shown (a bind is minutes per part). Captions are 32px on one line so they never cover the remote. ab's glass remote (desktop_demo_panel id fusion-tour) drives it: play, pause, next, back, mute, unmute, X = stop, with an instant loopback callback plus a poll backstop, one FIFO for the panel and fusion_demo_control, an ack caption per press; captions narrate every beat and pre-rendered narration audio plays locally (mute is session-only, unmute replays the beat). Every beat is measured before it moves (front, title, painted, stable) and then moves (2D zoom through the add-in, 3D orbit and zoom through Fusion's camera, verified by capture). Returns {demoId, estimatedSec, steps} at once; fusion_demo_progress {demoId} carries step, beatIndex/beatCount, percent, paused, muted, stopping, panel, presses[], captions[], per-step verified/placed/foregrounded/motion, shots[] (one evidence frame per beat), windowsRestored and tourDocsClosed. Fusion is placed on 80% of the primary work area for the show and restored at the end. Pass legacy:true for the previous step-list tour.

verbs.name: fusion_install_library_bundle
verbs.summary: COMPOSITE, the Fusion twin of kicad_install_library_bundle (#68): ONE call takes a staged Cloud Library bundle (zip of <Lib>.lbr + <Part>.step models, or a bare lbrPath with STEPs beside it), unpacks it safely, places it under ~/Documents/Adom Libraries/<name>/, pairs EVERY deviceset with its STEP by name (deviceset, package, normalised, prefix; a one-part library pairs its single model regardless), lints part numbers (partMetadata: MPN, manufacturer, Mouser/DigiKey/LCSC - reported, never blocking), pre-flights Fusion state (fusion{status}), and starts the same bind -> prove chain fusion_create_library runs. ASYNC BY CONTRACT: returns IMMEDIATELY with runId + statusVerb because a STEP bind is 3-15 minutes and cannot fit a relay window; poll fusion_prove_result (measured percent, four streamed proof frames per part, provedParts[], and an addin_restart_required payload the CALLER turns into the ask). PARTIAL SHIPS: a deviceset with no model is a NAMED skip in unbound[], the rest still bind; partsBound < partsTotal is the signal. Each part is minted on its own single-deviceset library (the Package3D generator loads the FIRST package of the open library, so a merged library would put every chip on part one's footprint), with the STEP placed exactly as published (orient:false, origin trusted), then all urns are bound into the merged library, and after prove the bound library is SAVED TO THE CLOUD under <project>/Adom Libraries so it appears in Fusion's Library Manager (cloudLibrary{saved, fileId, duplicatesBefore} in fusion_prove_result). Per-part scaffolding is deleted; the user is left with one library plus its per-package f3d folder. capture:false only places the files and returns. This is the one contract the wiki CLI (`library install --format fusion`) and the Export button both read; the recipe has one owner.

For an EE this is the point of the library: two variants can share ONE symbol, ONE footprint and ONE 3D body and still be different products (an AEC-Q100 automotive part vs the baseline one), and that difference lives ENTIRELY in the metadata. EAGLE spells the orderable identity as deviceset + device + technology: <device> carries the PACKAGE variant, <technology> carries the GRADE/temperature variant, and attributes hang off <technology>. Reports per-variant MPN / MANUFACTURER / MOUSER_PN / DIGIKEY_PN / LCSC_PN (the exact names this bridge's own BOM export reads), plus warnings when variants are indistinguishable, share an MPN, or a deviceset has no description. verbs.summary: Import a legacy EAGLE .sch (+ paired .brd) into a NEW Fusion electronics design so the parts INSTANTIATE (schematic + populated board, lands in the PCB editor). The ONLY way to author a board from EAGLE source: Document.newDesignFromLocal opens the schematic editor but does NOT instantiate parts, and the Fusion-native .fsch/.fbrd container is opaque binary you can't build offline. This fires Fusion's own ImportSCHAndBRDCmd and drives BOTH native Open dialogs (the .sch then the .brd) in the BACKGROUND via desktop_ui_click by accessible name (no foreground). Stage both files to Windows first (send_files). After: fusion_show_2d_board, RATSNEST + 'AUTO ;' to autoroute, fusion_show_3d_board for 3D. PREFLIGHT (1.10.20): refuses with eagle_files_missing before touching any dialog when either file is not on the Fusion machine; if the Open dialog does not accept the file the bridge cancels the dialog itself (open_dialog_stuck), so nothing is ever left on the user's screen. Prefer fusion_schematic {action:"open"}, which picks this route only when a .brd exists next to the .sch. ASYNC by contract (1.10.22): returns {started:true, runId, statusVerb} at once and runs the dialog-driven import on the exe; poll fusion_eagle_import_status {runId}. The record and the final reply carry documentName, partsExpected (elements in the .brd) and partsPlaced (read back from the board); success needs parts on the board (nothing_instantiated otherwise). Pass wait:true only from inside the exe.

verbs.name: fusion_plan_library_import
verbs.summary: PRE-FLIGHT for a library import: does NO work and changes nothing. Reports whether Fusion is installed, running, or needs its add-in loaded (with a plain-language message you can show the user), plus a per-stage plan with MEASURED per-machine time estimates scaled to the number of parts you are sending - a multi-part library does one STEP import per part, which is the slowest stage, so the estimate grows with the library. Call this FIRST so the wiki can render the summary and the progress bar's steps, then run the import and poll fusion_prove_result, which reports the SAME stage names.

verbs.name: fusion_pour_state
verbs.summary: Read every pour on the live board with Fusion's own computed fill: filled area per pour, per layer and per net, and which pours were never filled (no RATSNEST since they were drawn). The measure step of the AI flow's Fusion lane.

verbs.name: fusion_preflight_lbr
verbs.summary: PRE-ANALYZE a .lbr: will Fusion open it? Offline and instant - no Fusion needed, nothing launched. Runs the named checks the bridge learned from real Fusion rejections: file-readable, size-sane (truncated-transfer corpse detection), xml-parses, root-is-eagle, packages-nonempty (Fusion's silent 'No Components'), symbols-present, devicesets-present (missing ones make EDIT raise Create-new prompts), connects-resolve (dead wiring renders fine and connects nothing). fusion_open_lbr and fusion_create_library run the same gate automatically; call this directly to gate a batch BEFORE staging.

verbs.name: fusion_prefs_close
verbs.summary: Apply+OK (save:true, the default) or Cancel Fusion's Preferences dialog. Settings changed via fusion_prefs_open are NOT persisted until this is called with save:true.

verbs.name: fusion_prefs_open
verbs.summary: Open Fusion's Preferences dialog and optionally jump to a section, then hand back a SCREENSHOT + shotId you can click in. This is how you reach ANY Fusion preference: the Python API exposes only a thin slice (theme/orbit/units, debuggingPort, developer tools) and everything else, including the MCP server toggle, is UI-only. Sections: general, api, design, manufacture, electronics, render, drawing, material, graphics, network, preview features. Child sections under General are lazily rendered by Qt and never appear in the UIA tree, which is why this returns an image to click rather than control names. ALWAYS finish with fusion_prefs_close {save:true} - nothing is saved otherwise, and killing/restarting Fusion first discards the change.

verbs.name: fusion_prewarm
verbs.summary: Warm the bridge ahead of the first real call, WITHOUT starting Fusion: confirms the add-in is synced into every Fusion add-in folder, readies the space-free staging folder, and caches the PCB design-rules catalog from adom/pcb-design-rules. Adom Bridge calls it once per installed version in the background (bridge.json prewarm.verb); safe to call again any time. Launching Fusion is never part of it.

verbs.name: fusion_prove_result
verbs.summary: POLL a background run started by fusion_create_library or the detached fusion_build_library_3d. Returns stage + stageLabel, plan[] with measured per-stage estimates, stagesDone, percent, etaSec, confidence, and evidence[] filling in AS EACH ARTIFACT LANDS (symbol -> footprint -> 3d -> ganged). For a 3D build it carries per-part progress (minting X (3/7)), partsDone/partsTotal and parts[] with each wip_urn. stage:done only means the chain FINISHED - the top-level verdict (proven/not_proven) is the score, and a run that captured zero frames lands stage:failed with blocked_by_dialog (carrying the dialog text) or no_evidence_captured rather than reporting done. Pass inlineFrames:true on the final fetch for base64 thumbnails a browser can render. restarts[] {at, why, kind} lists any restart the chain performed (only with allowRestart). prove.planned / prove.skipped say whether evidence frames were captured and why (AI threads bind only by default).

Call this before driving Fusion; if installed-but-not-running, fusion_start. SELF-HEALS the seat/licensing dialog (background UIA + screenshot-verify) whenever it detects one. Pairs with ab's bridge_readiness.

The counterpart of fusion_claim_seat.

verbs.name: fusion_reset_workspace
verbs.summary: Bring Fusion back to a clean slate between runs: closes named documents AND the Untitled scratch the library/bind flow leaves behind (page issue #59). Fusion always keeps ONE blank document alive, so a single remaining Untitled is correct rather than a failure. MODIFIED Untitled docs are left untouched unless force:true, because those can hold real unsaved work.

verbs.name: fusion_resolve_seat_dialog
verbs.summary: Readiness EXECUTOR (Rust port, Phase 3): detect + resolve the Autodesk seat/licensing modal ('Active Sessions Exceeded' / 'Suspend Remote Session') in the background, at most 3 UIA clicks per call, screenshot-verified. Idempotent: nothing up answers clicks:0. fusion_readiness calls this itself when it sees the dialog; call it directly only when you are driving the launch by hand.

verbs.name: fusion_restart_for_addin
verbs.summary: ASYNC: returns immediately (started:true) and restarts Fusion in the background, SAVING the user's open documents first; poll fusion_readiness until ready with the new addinVersion (a restart takes 60-120s, longer than the relay budget; pass wait:true for the old blocking form). Finish add-in setup by restarting Fusion. Call this when any verb returns errorCode addin_restart_required (the add-in was installed/updated while Fusion was already open, and Fusion only loads add-ins at launch). ASK THE USER FIRST when a human is present - the failing verb's payload carries userMessage plus openDocuments/unsavedDocuments so you can show them what is open. Refuses with unsaved_named_document rather than discarding a never-saved document.

verbs.name: fusion_ripup_nets

verbs.name: fusion_routing_state

verbs.summary: START HERE for a schematic. Every reply says which underlying verb it used (via). Remember: a schematic is a VIEW of an electronics design, not a file of its own, which is why there is no verb called open_a_schematic_file. To put a library's parts on a NEW schematic and board for showing them off, use fusion_make_showcase_project instead.

Pure computation from the .lbr; nothing in Fusion changes.

Anything else is refused before the first command runs. ADD is proven against libraryPath on disk first (the deviceset must be there; the library is USEd by the bridge), so the component picker can never open. Readback: the parts and nets on the sheet from a fresh export.

Every fusion_readiness call checks for that offer and, if present, the bridge clicks it IN THE BACKGROUND (UIA, no foreground, no caption) so the download starts and the newer build comes up on the next launch. The user should never have to click it. Call with no args to read the current setting; {enabled:false} opts out and the choice is STICKY (~/.adom/fusion-bridge/prefs.json) - once a user opts out, NEVER click their update prompts again. verbs.name: fusion_signin
verbs.summary: SELF-DRIVING as of 1.9.32: launches Fusion if needed, clicks Sign In, opens the OAuth in the right profile, TYPES THE EMAIL and advances to the exact remaining wall (password/2FA/handoff), toasting the user at that step only - see signinWall + _hint in the response, and the fusion-autodesk-signin skill. Sign Fusion in through the CORRECT browser profile - the fix for Fusion's dumb OAuth that fires at the OS-DEFAULT browser and lands in the wrong Autodesk account. Fusion opens its sign-in in whatever browser is default (e.g. a personal Chrome), but a user's Autodesk seat often lives in a different profile (work). This verb reads the FULL authorize URL (client_id/PKCE/state/request_id) that Fusion wrote into that wrong browser's HISTORY and re-opens it in the RIGHT profile IN THE BACKGROUND; the URL completes back to the running Fusion via the idmgr/callback + autodesk:// handoff, so the browser no longer has to be the OS default. Pass {profile:'chrome:you@work.com'} to fix + remember your Autodesk profile; else it probes each profile for a live Autodesk session (or asks). Staged: if Fusion hasn't opened the browser yet it returns stage:'click_signin' so you click Fusion's Sign In first. BEST: pass {auto:true} to run the WHOLE chain in ONE server-side call - it clicks Fusion's Sign In, polls the browser history on-box for the fresh authorize URL, and re-opens it in the target profile, all without extra remote round-trips, so it fits inside Fusion's ~2-min OAuth request expiry even on a slow/flaky relay (the manual staged path is the fallback). Fusion's request EXPIRES in ~2 min, so a stale captured URL returns stage:'stale' - restart Fusion (fusion_stop/start) for a fresh request and retry auto PROMPTLY. See the 'fusion-multiprofile-signin' skill.

input.code: required str (the 6 digits; non-digits are stripped)

verbs.name: fusion_signin_2fa
verbs.summary: Submit Autodesk's emailed 6-DIGIT verification code to finish a Fusion sign-in, typed IN THE BACKGROUND (UIA SetValue + Invoke - never steals the user's foreground or moves their cursor). Exists so you can finish a login END TO END for the user instead of parking them on a 2FA screen: if `adom-google` is available in your container, read the code out of their Gmail (`adom-google gmail search 'from:autodesk verification code' --limit 1`), pull the 6 digits, and call this. If adom-google is NOT installed, tell the user that installing it would let you automate logins like this, then let them type it. NEVER ask the user for a code you could read yourself. The bridge ALSO toasts the user's desktop whenever it hits a human wall, so you do not need to ask it to.

verbs.name: fusion_uninstall
verbs.summary: CASCADE CLEANUP, called by ab's bridge_uninstall BEFORE this bridge's cache is deleted (ab 2.0.35+). Removes the artifacts this bridge planted OUTSIDE its cache: the Fusion ADD-IN in Autodesk's AddIns directories (all three historical locations), plus this bridge's prefs (~/.adom/fusion-bridge) and APS OAuth tokens (~/.adom/fusion-aps). This matters more here than for most bridges: a stale AdomBridge add-in keeps loading on every Fusion launch and binding its port long after the bridge is gone. Fusion itself is never touched. Pass dryRun:true to see exactly what would be removed. If Fusion is RUNNING it holds the add-in files open, so removal may fail - the response says so and names the remedy.

verbs.summary: Sign a pup browser window into an Autodesk WEB surface (library.io, the hub portal at <hub>.autodesk360.com, Autodesk Account) via Google SSO. Fusion's DESKTOP app being signed in does NOT sign these in - they are separate web sessions.
